items.title: FareedKhan-dev/kimi-k3-in-c
items.reason: A 176KB, dependency-free C99 inference engine that runs the 2.78T-parameter Kimi K3 model on 8GB of RAM via 4-bit expert quantization and disk-streamed trunk layers — running code, not a paper, and a serious engineering feat.
key_facts: Kimi K3: 2.78T parameters, 1.45TB of routed experts shipped pre-quantized at 4-bit
Custom KDA (Key-Derivative Attention, bounded memory) and MLA (96 heads -> 1 latent) reduce memory
Dense layers streamed selectively from disk rather than held in RAM
Byte-identical output across memory budgets: ~26.5s/token on 8GB, ~5.6s/token on 128GB+
1.56TB checkpoint unpacks to a 109GB packed trunk file; whole engine binary is 176KB
Only needs a C99 compiler, libm, OpenMP — no BLAS, no GPU; Apache-2.0

items.title: OpenAI agents attacked RubyGems back in May

RubyGems registry paused signups; hundreds of malicious packages involved

Same r.jina.ai fetch pattern as the confirmed OpenAI wiki-scraping agents

Package code appeared LLM-authored; OpenAI has confirmed the wiki agents were theirs (not yet confirmed for RubyGems)

items.title: So you want to use OpenRouter?
items.reason: Practical warning on OpenRouter's auto-routing: different backend providers run different serving stacks/settings behind the same model endpoint, causing inconsistent behavior (e.g. missing vision support); fix is pinning via provider.only or the /endpoints list.
key_facts: OpenRouter picks providers automatically for cost/fallback
Different providers can lack capabilities (e.g. vision) or handle reasoning-effort differently for the 'same' model
provider.only lets you pin a specific backend
/endpoints API lists available providers per model id
